title: Frozen Lemon Posset
description: A traditional British posset — sweetened cream set by lemon juice — frozen instead of chilled. The freezer turns the soft pudding into a dense, custardy semi-frozen dessert.

directions.title: Simmer
directions.text: Simmer the heavy cream with a pinch of salt, the sugar, and the lemon zest for 3-5 minutes.

directions.title: Set
directions.text: Pull off the heat and whisk in the lemon juice. Rest 10 minutes.

directions.title: Strain
directions.text: Strain to pull the zest out. Microplaned zest is not pleasant to eat.

directions.title: Freeze
directions.text: Pour into ramekins (or hollowed-out lemon halves) and freeze about 4 hours. Serve straight from the freezer.

notes: Worth trying with other citrus. Lime is close to a straight swap. Blood orange would need its acid bumped — supplement with lemon juice — since it isn't tart enough on its own to set the cream.

deviations.why: A traditional posset sets in the fridge into a soft, spoonable pudding. Freezing it gives a denser, custardy semi-frozen texture.

deviations.what: Heavier on the lemon than a typical posset
deviations.why: Slightly more zest and juice than standard, pushing the lemon flavor further forward.
